newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Svyazinvest sees telecoms decree in 10 days.
newsitem.headline: Svyazinvest sees telecoms decree in 10 days.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin is likely to issue a single decree within 10 days authorising the sale of 49 percent of Russian state telecoms holding company Svyazinvest and the transfer of 38 percent of long-distance operator Rostelekom to Svyazinvest, the head of Svyazinvest said on Friday.

"We expect a document will appear within 10 days authorising the transfer of shares including Rostelekom, Central Telegraph, Giprosvyaz and Yekaterinburg City Telephone," Nail Izmailov, chief executive of AO Svyazinvest, told a CS First Boston investment conference.
In answer to questions, Izmailov said the document would be a single presidential decree which would also authorise sales of 25 percent and 24 percent of Svyazinvest.

The government is planning to sell 25 percent of Svyazinvest, which owns controlling stakes in 85 regional telecommunications companies, to foreign buyers and 24 percent to Russians, seeking portfolio rather than strategic investors.
A previous attempt to tender 25 percent of Svyazinvest to strategic foreign investors, won by Italy's Stet Spa in late 1995, subsequently fell through.
The 38 percent stake in Rostelekom amounts to a controlling stake of 51 percent of the voting shares, and will create a single entity in the Russian telecoms sector.
But Rostelekom officials say they expect to retain operational independence after the merger.
